records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a) to (c):	A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>******<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>STATEMENT IN REPLY TO THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.*34 FOR 27.04.2016.<br/><br/>(a):	In 2009, the Government had decided to raise the strength of BSF by raising 29 additional battalions and of CRPF by 38 additional battalions in a phased manner. records.qtitle: Changes in MGNREGA
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government proposes to increase the employment days under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)<br/>in near future; and<br/><br/>(b) 	what other changes Government proposes to incorporate in the scheme to improve the living conditions of the rural poor?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI BIRENDER SINGH)<br/><br/>(a):	Yes Sir. The Government is actively engaged with State Governments in establishing systems that ensure provision of work as per demand, transparency and accountability. To generate awareness about the provisions of the Scheme and to provide adequate employment opportunities to rural households under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), the States/UTs have been requested for the following:	<br/><br/>(i)	Initiate appropriate IEC campaigns including wall paintings for wide dissemination of the   provisions of the Act.<br/><br/>(ii)	Expand scope and coverage of demand registration system to ensure that demand for work under MGNREGA does not go unregistered.<br/><br/>(iii)	Organize ‘Rozgar Diwas’ periodically to capture latent demand under the programme and to disseminate awareness about the provisions of the Act.<br/><br/>(iv)	Formulation of a specific plan to include special categories of vulnerable people viz. persons with disabilities, primitive tribal groups, nomadic tribal groups, de-notified tribes etc.<br/><br/>(b):	Following are the interventions by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) that, as incorporated will improve the living conditions of the rural poor.<br/><br/>(i)	A Convergent Planning Approach using the Socio Economic Cast Census (SECC) Data: Utilising SECC data ensures sharper focus and targeting of the excluded rural poor. Secondly, convergent planning ensures that benefits of rural development programs do not reach the beneficiaries in silos but in alignment and convergence. Thus, living conditions of the rural poor is expected to improve both at the household as well as the GP level.<br/><br/>(ii)	The clear formulation of targets for assets: The current interventions of MoRD are focussed with clear targets that would clearly improve sustainable livelihoods, focus on sustainable interventions relating to land, water and trees and facilitate in creating rural infrastructure.<br/><br/>(iii)	Capacity building of grassroots level functionaries through projects like Cluster Facilitation teams, Barefoot Technician and Technical Training through District Technical Resource Team and Block Technical Resource Team.<br/><br/>*****<br/>	<br/>

records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text: (a) the number of communal violence occurred in the country during the last four months, month-wise and location-wise;<br/><br/>(b) the loss of life and property in each case; and<br/><br/>(c) the major causes of the incidents?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a) and (b): As per available information, state-wise details of number of communal incidents reported in the country and number of persons killed during July to October, 2015 is enclosed at Annexure.<br/><br/> “Public Order” and “Police” are State subjects as per the provisions of the Constitution of India. records.qtitle: BPL families in Kerala getting subsidized foodgrains
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text: (a) 	the number of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families registered in Kerala getting subsidized foodgrains;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether it is a fact that the actual number of BPL families in Kerala is much more than registered; and<br/><br/>(c) 	if so, the steps taken by Government in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION<br/>(SHRI RAM  VILAS PASWAN)<br/><br/>(a) to (c):   For allocation of foodgrains (rice & wheat) to States and Union Territories (UTs) under the existing TPDS, Department of Food and Public Distribution uses the number of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families based on 1993-94 poverty estimates of Planning Commission and the population estimates of Registrar General of India (RGI) as on 1st March 2000 or the number of such families actually identified and ration cards issued to them by State/UT Governments, whichever is less.  As per these estimates, the accepted number of BPL families in the State of Kerala is 15.54 lakh, including 5.96 AAY families. However, the State Government has identified more BPL families and reported issuance of 20.77 lakh BPL ration cards including 5.96 lakh AAY ration cards in the State for allocation of foodgrains under TPDS.  <br/><br/>          Government of India is allocating monthly quantity of 54384 tons of foodgrains to Kerala for the above accepted BPL families, including AAY families @ 35 kg per family per month as per existing TPDS norms.   To meet their additional requirements, the Government has been making additional allocation of foodgrains to the State for additional BPL families since 2010-11.  During the current year, Kerala has been allocated 59586 tons of foodgrains at BPL rates for distribution to the additional BPL families for a period of six months from April to 30th September, 2015 or till implementation of National Food Security Act (NFSA) in the State, whichever is earlier.<br/>.<br/>***<br/> <br/>

Names of crops notified under NAIS during Kharif & Rabi seasons are given in Annexure.<br/><br/>(b):	Comprehensive risk insurance is provided due to non-preventable risks including failure of seeds under NAIS.  As the scheme is being implemented on area approach basis, the admissible claims are settled on the basis of final yield data furnished by the State Government for the notified area and crop.<br/> <br/>

records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS<br/>[GEN. (DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD)]<br/><br/>(a) & (b) 	The Government has already put in place an express passport service called ‘Tatkal Scheme’ which was introduced on 1st January 2000 in all the Passport Offices in India.<br/><br/>(c) 	As on 30th June 2015, a total of 4,86,080 passport applications (out of 52.66 lakh applications received and processed) are pending at all the Passport Offices for various reasons such as : i) awaiting verification/granting at Passport Seva Kendras and Passport Offices; ii) awaiting confirmation of genuineness of Verification Certificates; iii) on account of adverse Police Verification Reports; and, iv) awaiting printing and postal delivery. <br/><br/>(d)	Though it is the endeavour of the Ministry to provide timely passport service, issuance of passport depends upon various factors such as proper verification of identity documents and clear Police verification reports covering citizenship status, criminality status and antecedents of the applicant. records.qtitle: Functioning of Waqf Boards in various States
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text: (a)   the number of Waqf Boards functioning at present in various States;<br/><br/>(b)   the details of Waqf properties under the control of such boards; <br/><br/>(c)   the estimated cost of properties under each board; and <br/><br/>(d)   the nature of control of the Central Government on the Waqf Boards?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF MINORITY AFFAIRS<br/>              (SHRI MUKHTAR ABBAS NAQVI)<br/><br/><br/>(a):	There are 30 State/UT Waqf Boards are functioning at present in various States.<br/><br/>(b)&(c):	According to Section 32(1) of the Waqf Act, 1995, the general superintendence of all auqaf in a State shall vest in the Board established by the State/UT Government and it shall be the duty of the Board so to exercise its power under this Act as to ensure the auqaf under its superintendence are properly maintained, controlled and administered and the income thereof is duly applied to the objects and for the purposes for which such auqaf were created and intended. Accordingly, no such details of waqf properties and estimated cost of properties are maintained by the Central Government.<br/><br/>(d):  	As per Section 13 (1) of the Waqf Act, 1995, State Waqf Boards are established by the State Government by notification in the Official Gazette. Thus, State Waqf Boards are not directly controlled by the Central Government. However, Central Waqf Council which is an Advisory Body of the Central Government suggests/advises the State waqf Boards as and when require/ deemed necessary. <br/><br/>                         ********<br/>

records.qtitle: SELECTION OF HAJ PILGRIMS .

(b) the details thereof;

(d) whether they would get a chance for Haj?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(DR. SHASHI THAROOR)

(a) & (b) In accordance with the Haj Agreement signed with the Government of Saudi Arabia, the Haj quota is allotted between the Haj Committee of India (HCOI) and the Private Tour Operators (PTOs). Subsequently, HCOI allocates its quota among various States on the basis of the percentage of Muslim population in the States as per 2001 census. HCOI then invites applications from the intending pilgrims and thereafter the selection is made through a computerized qurrah (draw of lots). The quota can be availed under this category only once in five years.

(c) & (d) The matter regarding priority for those Haj applicants who had applied for several consecutive years but not been selected is under the consideration of the Government.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SHRI DINESH TRIVEDI)

(a) to (c) An Indian student who graduates from a Medical Institution abroad has to follow the procedure to get permanent registration, entitlement for practice and further studies in India:

(i) Obtain eligibility certificate issued by the Medical Council of India at the time of admission;

(ii) Appear for Screening Test conducted by National Board of Examinations;

(iii) On successful completion of Screening Test, provisional registration for internship training is awarded by the Medical Council of India;

(iv) After completion of internship training, permanent registration is granted by the Medical Council of India.

records.qtitle: OUT OF SCHOOL CHILDREN IN ABSENCE OF CRECHE FACILITIES
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of children in the age group of 6-14 years for whom education has been made a Fundamental Right are still out of school, particularly in the slum areas in metropolitan cities;

(b) if so, whether any survey has recently been conducted to assess their number, if so, the details thereof, State-wise; and

(c) the manner in which this problem, particularly of children in this age group, in metropolitan cities and areas around them, whose parents are unable to send them to school as there are no creche facilities for their younger siblings and their parents are out for work during the day, is proposed to be tackled?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) & (b) As per independent sample survey commissioned by Ministry of Human Resource Development, the estimated number of out of school children is 81.5 lakh, of which 1.36 lakh children were out of school in slums of urban areas. A statement indicating the total estimated State wise number of out of school children in the age group 6-14 years, and out of school children in slum areas is given in the Annexure.

(c) Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) follows a holistic approach for universal access and retention, bridging of gender and social category gaps in Education and improving the quality of education for all children, including children in slum areas in urban and metropolitan cities. The interests of out of school children in urban slums are addressed through Education Guarantee Centres (EGS), Residential Bridge Courses and Non-Residential Bridge Courses. Early Child Care and Education (ECCE) is a critical and essential input for freeing girls from sibling care responsibilities. SSA emphasizes the importance of strengthening convergence with the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Programme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

records.qtitle: BAN ON ONLINE LOTTERIES
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Kerala Government has sought a ban on online lotteries;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the action taken thereon?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI AJAY MAKEN)

(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.


STATEMENT IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.398 FOR 16.12.2009 REGARDING “BAN ON ONLINE LOTTERIES”

(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. The Government of Kerala has represented that there should be a ban on online lottery. They have also represented that a law should be made for online lottery with freedom to State Government to ban it, if Government of India does not desire to ban it nationally.

(c): The Government of India had on 23.12.1999 introduced Lotteries (Prohibition) Bill, 1999 in Rajya Sabha, which seeks to prohibit the organization, conduct and promotion of lotteries falling under Entry 40 of List-I – Union List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. The Bill was referred to the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Ministry of Home Affairs for examination and report. The Committee in its report suggested that the Government may take up the issue of banning the lotteries at the political level and explore possibilities of evolving a larger consensus in the matter.
In a bid to evolve political consensus on the Lotteries (Prohibition) Bill, 1999, various efforts were made by the Ministry and finally the overwhelming view which emerged was that “the lotteries should not be prohibited, but there should be stronger and more effective regulation of lotteries”.
Consequently, the Central Government decided to withdraw the Lotteries (Prohibition) Bill, 1999. The matter for withdrawal of the Bill was discussed in the Rajya Sabha on 24.11.2009, but the Motion to withdraw the Bill was deferred.

records.qtitle: WOMEN INMATES LODGED IN PRISONS .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the names of States where women inmates are housed in prisons exclusively built for them;

(b) whether Centre has given any directions to the States in this regard; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN)

(a): As per the statistics complied by National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), as on 31.12.2007, there were 12 states viz. Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Kerala, Maharashtra, Orissa, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Delhi where women inmates are housed in prisons exclusively built for them.

(b) & (c): “Prisons” is a state subject under List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India and Prison Administration is primarily the responsibility of the respective State Governments. However, the Union Government from time to time has been advising the State Governments and Union Territories for the betterment of women prisoners during their custody in terms of their special needs and to maintain their human dignity. It has also been advised to have separate prison for women offenders wherever feasible. At other places, the women prisoners shall be kept in a strictly secluded female enclosures/wards.

(SHRI PRADEEP JAIN `ADITYA`)

Evaluation of every rural development programme, including the employment generation schemes are done periodically through independent agencies. The Ministry has engaged Professional Institutions like Indian Institute of Technologies (IITs), Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs), Agricultural Universities and other Social Sector Institutions for independent evaluation and impact assessment of NREGA.

records.qtitle: LOANS TO MUSLIMS .

The banks follow guidelines issued by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) from time to time on Priority Sector Lending/Credit Facilities to Minority Communities. There is no mandatory requirement of furnishing guarantee by Government officials for grant of loans to Muslims.

records.qtitle: NATIONAL STOCK EXCHANGE .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that National Stock Exchange (NSE) is promoted by the Public Sector Institutions which together hold a majority stake therein;

(b) what is the cash component (i.e .non-fixed deposit and non-bank Guarantee of the Settlement Guarantee Fund of NSE for all its segments;

(c) what are the fields in which the money has been invested by NSE and what is the composition of the body which takes decision for investment; and

(d) what is the frequency period prescribed for the meetings of the investment body?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINACE

(NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) to (d): There is no holding by either Central or State Government in the equity shares of National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE). Public sector banks and insurance companies hold less than 50 per cent of paid up equity share capital of NSE. As informed by NSE, the cash component of Settlement Guarantee Fund (SGF) for all segments is Rs. 1076.15 crore as on March 31, 2009. For the day to day treasury management including the cash management of the SGF, the investments are made in debt instruments like Bank Fixed Deposits, units of various schemes of debt and liquid mutual funds, taxable/tax free bonds, etc. as per the prudential policy laid down by the Board of NSE. The composition of the Board of NSE is enclosed at Annexure.

records.qtitle: MUSLIMS BELOW POVERTY LINE .

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the schemes formulated to ameliorate the economic status of Muslims?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF MINORITY AFFAIRS

(SALMAN KHURSHID)

(a) No, Sir.

(b) Does not arise.

(c) National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation (NMDFC), a Public Sector Enterprise under the administrative control of Ministry of Minority Affairs, provides loans at concessional rates for self employment / income generating activities to persons belonging to the minority communities living below double the poverty line, under its various schemes viz. Term Loan, Micro Financing, Mahila Samridhi Yojana, Vocational Training and Marketing Assistance etc. NMDFC provides loans to individuals through State Channelising Agencies (SCAs) which are nominated by the respective State/UT Governments. It also provides micro-credit through Non-governmental Organizations (NGOs).

The scheme of Multi-Sectoral Development Programme being implemented by the Government aims, inter alia, at improving the selected socio-economic and basic amenities’ parameters in the Minority Concentration Districts (MCDs) during the Eleventh Five Year Plan period. The Government is also implementing coaching/scholarship schemes for students belonging to minority communities which aim to equip them for engaging in income generating activities.

However, the Government has started the process of developing a common perspective on the issue of voluntary affirmative action by the corporate sector, and recently an interaction with the representatives of corporate sector and related stakeholders was organized jointly by the Confederation of Indian Industry and the National Foundation for Corporate Governance.

Annexure

Statement referred to in reply to the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 67 by Shri Abdul Wahab Peevee, MP for answer on 8.7.2009 regarding “Centre’s caution to Kerala about law and order problem”.


(a) to (c) : As per the Constitution, “Public Order” and “Police” are State subjects and it is primarily the responsibility of the State Governments to maintain law and order in their States. However, the Central Government reviews the internal security situation in the country from time to time. During such a security review the issue of more effective policing in certain areas of Malappuram and Tiruvananthapuram, came up for discussion. The State Government has been advised to take necessary action in this regard.

records.qtitle: ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW COLLEGES .

records.ans_text:

(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.52 FOR 7.7.2009, ASKED BY SHRI ABDUL WAHAB PEEVEE, HON’BLE MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT, REGARDING ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW COLLEGES.

(a) to (d): There is a proposal to launch a new scheme with Central-State funding for establishment of one model degree college in each of the 374 identified educationally backward districts having Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) lower than the national GER. These include 62 districts identified by the Ministry of Minority Affairs as minority concentration districts where the population of the minority group is over 20% on the basis of the 2001 census data on population, and have poor socio-economic indicators and basic amenities indicators, 17 districts where minorities constitute 20% or more of the population and 36 districts which are dominated by those who are religious minorities nationally but are a majority in the respective States.

During the remaining period of the XI Plan, subject to the approval of the competent authority, the Central Government proposes to provide some financial assistance for establishing 200 model colleges, in consultation with the concerned State Governments.

records.qtitle: SECURITIES AND BORROWING LENDING SCHEME .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the reasons for which the Securities and Borrowing Lending Scheme is not being rolled out in National Stock Exchange (NSE) properly;

(b) the reasons behind NSE promoting cash settled Futures and Options(F&O) which has led to excessive speculation;

(c) the reasons for which NSE is not implementing SEBI`s vision of the balance scheme of Securities and Borrowing Lending to protect its monopoly of cash settled F&O which as per original report were to be cash settled only for one year; and

(d) what percentage of NSE volume constitute cash settled Nifty futures and what NSE has done to deepen the Capital Markets in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) to (c): Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has provided a framework for Securities Lending & Borrowing (SLB) Scheme which has been operationalised with effect from April 21, 2008. NSE has accordingly implemented the scheme based on the framework provided by SEBI.
SEBI on October 31, 2008 has revised the framework for the SLB Scheme pursuant to feedback from market participants. The revision in framework for SLB Scheme inter-alia include increased timings for lending ~d borrowing, increased borrowing tenure, revision in margin methodology and handling of corporate action. NSE has reported that revising required considerable system changes to the existing set-up of SLB Scheme at NSE which has been done. It has been decided to implement the revised framework~ Currently, index futures, index options, stock futures and stock options are available for trading in the equity derivatives market. The current regulatory framework envisages cash settlement of all derivative contracts. As reported by NSE, there has been no issue faced with respect to settlement of cash settled derivatives contracts till date.

(d): For the past six months, on an average, Nifty futures .constituted around 32% and Nifty options around 35% of the total trading volumes in derivatives. NSE has taken various measures to deepen the capital market in the country including conducting investor awareness and education programs across the country, increased reach of participants by facilitating trading from locations across the country, updated its website providing detailed information, providing trade verification by clients through its website etc.

records.qtitle: TRADE BETWEEN INDIA AND SINGAPORE .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has any plan to increase the scope of import/export between India and Singapore in near future;

(b) if so, whether Government has taken up the matter with Singapore in this regard;

(c) whether Government has identified the items which are in great demand in Singapore and vice-versa;

(d) if so, the details thereof;

(e) whether Government propose to liberalize the import/export norms in this regard; and

(f) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a) to (f): A Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) between India and Singapore was signed on 29th June, 2005, which came into effect from 1st August, 2005. To further expand the tariff liberalization package within the Trade in Goods chapter, India and Singapore have signed a Protocol on 20-12-2007 to amend the India-Singapore CECA. Details of the agreement are available at www.commerce.nic.in/trade/international_ta_framework_ceca.asp. India-Singapore bilateral trade increased from US $ 6.65 billion in 2004-05 to US $ 15.49 billion in 2007-08 at a compounded annual growth rate of 32.53%. The top 5 items of export from India to Singapore during 2007-08 were; light oils and preparations, other petroleum oils & oils obtained from bituminous minerals etc., special transactions & commodities not classified according to kind, floating/ submersible drilling/ production platform and; aluminium-not alloyed.
Similarly, top 5 items of import from Singapore to India during 2007-08 were; other petroleum oils & oils obtained from bituminous minerals, self propelled boring/ sinking machinery, other vessels & floats etc., unused postage revenue / similar stamps of current & new issues stamps / impressed paper/ cheque from bank/ stock share certificate & similar title documents and; styrene.

records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Group of Ministers (GoM) had cleared the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2006 for raising FDI in Insurance Sector up to 49 percent; and

(b) if so, by when Government proposes to introduce the said Bill in Parliament?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a & b): Yes, Sir. The Group of` Ministers (GoM) has approved the proposed amendments with certain modifications and the same are to be placed before the Cabinet.

records.qtitle: OPENING OF DUTY FREE SHOPS .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a face that Government ~had revised the procedure for allotment of duty free shops at various airports in the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether it is also a fact that Government had recently opened a duty free shop at the arrival lounge at Wagah Border on contract basis; and

(d) if so, what was the procedure prescribed and followed in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) No Sir. The practice/procedure for licensing of Duty Free Shops by Customs at the airports in the country has not been revised in the recent past.

(b) Not applicable in view of (a) above.

(c) Yes Sir. A Private Warehouse license under Section 58 of the Customs Ace, 1962 has been granted to M/s Flemingo DFS Private Limited for opening a Duty Free Shop at Wagah Border (Land Customs Station-Attari Road).

(d) The Duty Free Shops are licensed as Private Warehouse under Section 58 of the Customs Ace, 196Z The approval for opening of Duty Free Shop at Wagah Border was given after getting the necessary approval from Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) and after furnishing of requisite bond with security as per prevalent instructions/guidelines.

records.qtitle: STATUS OF MODERNIZATION OF AIRPORTS .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the status of his Ministry`s plan to upgrade 24 airports by 2009 and 11 by 2010;

(b) whether Government is considering to change the terms of the modernisation programme; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION

(SHRI PRAFUL PATEL)
(a),(b)&(c):- The terminal building and airside works for 24 non metro airports are scheduled to be completed by 2009 and for 11 airports by 2010 as planned.

records.qtitle: SACHAR COMMITTEE DATA IN NCERT BOOKS .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the data provided by the Sachar Committee Report that examined the social, economic and educational status of Muslims in this country, have found their way into NCERT books this year; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M. A. A. FATMI)

(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Some of the data provided by the Sachar Committee Report have been mentioned in `Social and Political Life`, textbook for Class VIII and `Democratic Politics` textbook for Class X.

records.qtitle: RAILWAY COACH FACTORY AT KANJIKODE
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
the status of setting up of a proposed Rs.5,000 crore 
       Railway coach  factory at Kanjikode in Kerala?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(DR. R.VELU)

There is no proposal to set up Rail Coach Factory at Kanjikode in Kerala. However, there is a proposal to set up rail coach factory at Palakkad in Kerala. Detailed Project Report for setting up of coach factory at Palakkad is under consideration of Ministry of Railways where after approval of Planning Commission and Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs shall be sought before it is put up for Parliamentary approval.

records.qtitle: CUSTOMS DUTY ON EDIBLE OILSEEDS .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether farmers of Kerala growing coconut and edible oilseeds are affected due to changes in custom duty on edible oils;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) how the Government propose to compensate the farmers?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a to c): The Government of Kerala has informed that the changes made by the Government in the import-policy on edible oils has severely affected the coconut farmers and therefore, requested to restore the tariff on import of palm oil to previous levels and permit export of coconut oil.

Accordingly, restrictions on export of Coconut Oil have been lifted for exports through Cochin Port. The Government has also exempted from this export ban certain other oils produced from minor forest products with effect from 01.04.2008.

records.qtitle: SHORTAGE OF QUALIFIED STAFF IN ENGINEERING COLLEGES .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether many engineering colleges, mostly in southern States are facing problems of shortage of qualified staff;

(b) if so, the details thereof, particularly in Kerala; and

(c) the steps taken by Government in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)


(a) to (c): There is a shortage of teaching staff in the country, including the State of Kerala. As per the report of the Committee on “Faculty Development in Technical Education” constituted by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) under the Chairmanship of Prof. P. Rama Rao, the total shortage of teaching staff in engineering & technology, during 2005-06, for the country as a whole, was about 40,000. This shortage was estimated based on the AICTE norms of teacher to student ratio as 1:15. Considering the shortage of well- qualified technical faculty in the country, the age of superannuation of teachers in Central Institutions has been enhanced from 62 years to 65 years. They can further be reemployed after superannuation till the age of 70 years.

records.qtitle: SETTING UP OF ALIGARH COMPLEX
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government proposes to set up Aligarh complex modified on Aligarh Muslim University some State;

(b) if so, the places selected for this purpose; and

(c) the status of the proposal?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) to (c): Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) is governed an Act of Parliament. In term of Section 12(2) of the Act, the University is competent to decide on setting up Special Centres, specialized Laboratories or other institutions for research or institution subject, however, to becessary amendments to its Statutes, in availability of the requisite funds. The Executive council of AMU has decided, in the principle, to establish, in due course of time, five centers at Bhopal Katihar, Murshidabad and Pune. However, the University has not forwarded any proposal seeking necessary amendments to its Statutes.

records.qtitle: NEW RAILWAY LINES IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has received proposals for new railway line in Kerala;

(b) whether Government is aware that the Nilambur-Nanjangud railway line would greatly benefit the information technology industry in Kerala; and

(c) if so, whether Government proposes to sanction this line on priority basis?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R. VELU)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b) & (c): An updating survey for construction of Nilambur Road–Nanjangud new line has been completed recently. As per the survey report, cost of construction of 238.40 kms long new line has been assessed as Rs. 1742.109 crore with Rate of Return of (-) 5.907%. In view of a number of major IT industrial houses setting up industries in the States of Kerala and Karnataka, travel needs of their employees have also been taken into consideration in this report for the proposed new line for Nilambur Road–Nanjangud. Further consideration of this proposal would be possible once the decision on the results of the survey are finalised.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) UNSEASONAL RAIN IN SOUTH INDIA .
records.name: Rajeev Chandrasekhar
records.qn_text:
(a) whether an assessment has been made of the loss caused to crops, life and property due to unseasonal rain in southern States of the country during the month of March in this year;

(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise and commodity-wise; and

(c) the rescue operations, special economic package and the Central assistance given to the States, State-wise?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)


(a) to (c): The Ministry of Home Affairs is concerned in the matter and necessary information is being collected form them.

records.qtitle: BSNL MOBILE CONNECTIONS IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a vast mismatch between demand for BSNL mobile connections in the State of Kerala and the capacity of the organisation to give connections; and

(b) if so, how Government proposes to ease the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA)


(a) No, Sir. Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) is providing mobile connections in Kerala Circle on demand for the current year. In addition, purchase orders have already been placed for 10.15 lakh lines capacity expansion of mobile network in Kerala Circle.

(b) The connections are being provided on demand. The position will further improve on expansion of mobile network as stated in (a) above.

records.qtitle: MEDICAL TOURISM IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the schemes formulated by Government to give a big boost to tourism including medical tourism in the State of Kerala in near future;

(b) the details of tourism projects approved but not executed so far; and

(c) the status of each project?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM AND CULTURE (SMT. AMBIKA SONI)

(a) to (c) : Integrated development of tourism in the country is a continuous process. Ministry of Tourism has been providing Central Financial Assistance on the basis of project proposals received from the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations including the State of Kerala under the following schemes:

(i) Product/Infrastructure development of destinations/circuits

(ii) Large Revenue Generating projects

(iii) Fairs/festivals/events

(iv) Information Technology
Proposals which are received in accordance with the scheme guidelines, are processed on inter-se priority basis and funds released subject to availability.
The Ministry of Tourism also promotes tourism products including medical tourism in overseas markets through the website, brochures, Compact Discs, participation in travel fairs and distribution of publicity material.
During 2007-08, the following project proposals, which were complete as per guidelines have been sanctioned for Central Financial Assistance to the Government of Kerala:
Sr.No. Name of the project Amount (Rs. in lakh)

1. Development of Kodungalloor heritage Tourism circuit 361.75

2. Development of Pathiramanal Bio-park 499.61

3. Destination development of Wayanad 201.72

4. Development of Mangalam Dam as a tourist destination 461.67

5. Destination development of Kottakkunnu in Malappuram 440.25 6. Development of Malampuzha in Palakkad as a tourist 482.04 destination

7 Setting up of the Institute of Hotel Management, Catering 1000.00 Technology & Applied Nutrition at Kozhikode (Kerala)

8. Development of Nila Heritage Tourism Circuit 606.40 (Bharathapuzha River) in Malappuram and Thrissur District

9. Development of Eco-Tourism programme in Gavi, Pathanamthitta 20.05 District 10. Documentation of Fifty Traditional Architectural 25.00 Structures of South India 11. Creation of websites with virtual tour for 8 properties 25.82 TOTAL 4124.31

During the 10th Five Year Plan, Ministry of Tourism sanctioned projects worth Rs.13,809.94 lakh for development of tourism in the State of Kerala.
Execution of projects is the responsibility of the State Government of Kerala. Ministry of Tourism monitors physical and financial progress of the sanctioned projects through site visits and review meetings from time to time.

records.qtitle: INDIAN SOLDIERS IN JAILS OF PAKISTAN .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether some Indian soldiers are interned in Pakistan jails;

(b) whether it is also a fact that a Flag officer of the Indian Air Force, belonging to 20th squadron A-7 of the Indian Air Force has also been lodged in Pak jail since 1971;

(c) whether the relatives of the PoW (Prisoners of War) who hails from Kerala, has approached Government to trace the officer; and

(d) if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) &(b) 74 Missing Defence Personnel including 54 since 1971 are believed to be in jails in Pakistan. Shri K.P.Muraleedharan, a Flying Officer of Indian Air Force is believed to be amongst them.

(c)&(d) Yes. Government have received a representation from his sister. She has been informed of the efforts Government are making to trace Missing Defence Personnel in Pakistan.

records.qtitle: PLACES SELECTED FOR INCREASING RUBBER PRODUCTION .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has approved recently some projects to increase rubber production in the country; and

(b) if so, the places selected for the purpose?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)



(a) & ( b) : Yes, Sir. The Government has approved the Rubber Plantation Development Scheme and the Scheme for Rubber Development in North East with outlay of Rs.240.39 crore and Rs.173.05 crore respectively for implementation during the 11th Five Year Plan for increasing rubber production in the country. While the Rubber Plantation Development Scheme is operational in the traditional region comprising the States of Kerala and Tamil Nadu and also the non-traditional region like Karnataka, Goa, Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, etc., the Scheme for Rubber Development in North East

records.qtitle: GREENFIELD INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT AT KANNUR KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Central Government has cleared a proposal for setting up a new greenfield international airport in Kannur in Kerala through the public-private partnership route;

(b)if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether the proposed airport would also act as a cargo hub for perishable items;

(d)the estimated cost of the entire project;and

(e)by when the work is expected to start?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a)&(b) Yes, Sir. The Government has accorded `in-principle` approval for setting up a greenfield airport at Kannur, Kerala through Public Private Partnership (PPP) route.The airport will be built over 2000 acres of land and will have a single runway.

(c)Yes, Sir.

(d)&(e) As per the Techno Economic Feasibility Report submitted by Government of Kerala, the total project cost is Rs.929.5 Crores with expenditure planned over 30 years, of which Rs.455 Crores would be spent in the initial construction period of 3 years. The construction would start once the strategic partner is selected by the State Government.

records.qtitle: LOAN TO FARMERS AGAINST NSC KVP .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with HDFC Bank to provide loans to farmers through post offices against National Savings Certificate (NSC) and Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP) in some States;

(b) if so, the States identified for the purpose; and

(c) by when the scheme would be operationalized?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT TO BE LAID ON THE TABLE OF RAJYA SABHA IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO 316 FOR 20TH OF MARCH, 2008 REGARDING LOAN TO FARMERS AGAINST NSC/KVP.

(a) Some Postal Circles of the Department of Posts have entered into a tie up with HDFC Bank for forwarding loan applications against the National Savings Certificates and Kisan Vikas Patra to the aforementioned bank. The post office verifies the genuineness of the National Savings Certificates and Kisan Vikas Patra before forwarding the loan applications to the HDFC Bank.

(b) & (c) The details are given in the Annexure.

records.qtitle: PROBLEMS FACED BY RESIDENTS OF JANAKPURI NO.
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether his Ministry has recently received representations from some Members of Parliament regarding the problems faced by the residents of B-2B Block, Janakpuri, New Delhi; and

(b) if so, the action taken by Government thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a)&(b): Yes, Sir. The representation received through some Members of Parliament was initially forwarded to Delhi Development Authority (DDA) for necessary action. However, it was informed that the area in question has been transferred to Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) in 1981. Therefore, a copy of the representation has been referred to MCD for taking necessary action.

records.qtitle: NEW TV CENTRE PROJECTS IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text: The status of new T.V. centre projects and augmentation of existing T.V. centre in Kerala?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SHRI P. R. DASMUNSl)

No new TV Centre is presently envisaged in Kerala. The following projects of augmentation of existing TV Centres in Kerala have been sanctioned:

i) replacement of existing 100 Watt LPTs at six places by 500 Watt automode (1 +1) LPTs.

ii) upgradation of an interim HPT to permanent set up.

iii) provision of script News automation system at DDK, Thiruvananthpuram. Orders for part equipment have been placed.

records.qtitle: . DECLINE IN INDUSTRIAL GROWTH IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the industrial growth of the state of Kerala has decreased during the last three years, if so, the year-wise details thereof; and

(b) the steps taken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)

(a): The industrial growth, measured in terms of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) emanating from industry, released by the Central Statistical Organisation, was 6.5% in 2004-05, 8.9% in 2005-06 and 8.2% in 2006-07.

(b): Industrial Development is the primary responsibility of the State Governments concerned and the industrial growth in a State depends on the market conditions, availability of raw materials and other inputs, the infrastructure support, the overall industrial climate and the policy support available.
The Central Government supplements their efforts by various policy measures, and has put in place various policies to promote broad based industrial growth, which includes, inter-alia, delicensing of industrial capacity, liberalization of foreign trade regime to provide better access to inputs at competitive prices, rationalization and reduction in duty rates of customs and central excise, better infrastructure support, and liberal FDI regime, etc.

records.qtitle: SEA EROSIONS AT KERALA COAST .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is aware that coastal belt of Kerala is severely affected by sea erosions every year causing considerable loss of land and property;

(b) whether proposals for works related to coastal protection have been received from the State Government;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) the action taken by Government thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV)

(a) to (d) Yes Sir. A proposal of `Constructing sea wall in district Thrissur` at an estimated cost of Rs.3.00 crore was received from the State Government of Kerala. During X Plan, first instalment of central share amounting to Rs.50 lakhs was released to the Government of Kerala in March, 2004. The State Government has been requested to send the requisite information for release of 2nd instalment of Rs.1.75 crore. Besides the above, the 12th Finance Commission has also awarded an amount of Rs.175 crore to the State of Kerala for anti-sea erosion works (for the period of 2006-2010) to undertake constructions of sea walls and groynes in Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Alappuzha, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Manjeri, Kozhikode, Thalessery and Kasaragode Divisions.

records.qtitle: AIRPORT INFRASTRUCTURE IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government proposes to improve the infrastructure facilities at the airports in Kerala;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the amount earmarked for this purpose?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION

( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a) Yes Sir.

(b) & (c) Airports Authority of India (AAI) have undertaken various development works at Trivandrum and Calicut International airports. At Trivandrum International Airport, AAI have taken up development works like construction of state-of-the-art Integrated Terminal Building Complex with all modern amenities and facilities etc. at an estimated cost of Rs.245.58 crores. At Calicut International Airport, AAI have taken up extension & modification of International and domestic Terminal Buildings and associated works, expansion of apron and strengthening of runway including profile correction for operation of B-747-400 type of aircraft etc. at an estimated cost of Rs.117.07 crores.

records.qtitle: MENACE OF DRUG ADDICTION .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is aware of the growing menace of drug addiction in the country, particularly among the student community;

(b) if so, whether any nation-wide survey in this regard has been conducted;

(c) the particulars of existing drug de-addiction centres in various States, particularly in Kerala; and

(d) the grant-in-aid provided to each such centre, particularly in Kerala, during the last three years, year-wise?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT

(SMT. MEIRA KUMAR)


(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement referred to in reply to Part (a) to (d) of the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 255 for answer on 17.03.2008 regarding the Menace of drug addiction


(a) & (b) Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment is aware of the problems of social deviance in India and their manifestation also in the form of drug abuse. The Ministry, in collaboration with the United Nations Organization on Drug and Crime (UNDOC) conducts various thematic studies and surveys focusing on the pattern and extent of drug abuse. However, these studies/surveys do not suggest that addiction among students is increasing.

(c) A statement showing State/UT-wise number of De-addiction centres throughout the country is at Annexure-I.

(d) The information is being collected.

records.qtitle: EXCLUSIVE RAILWAY ZONE AND COACH WAGON FACTORY IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Kerala Government has submitted a memorandum to the Centre for sanctioning an exclusive railway zone and a coach and wagon factory for the State; and

(b) if so, the action taken by Government thereon?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R. VELU)


(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): New Zones are set up keeping in view factors like size, workload, accessibility, traffic pattern and other operating / administrative requirements etc. consistent with the needs of economy and efficiency without any regional considerations. While presenting the Railway Budget 2008-09, a new rail coach factory has been announced for the State of Kerala to meet the requirement of passenger coaches. However, there is no proposal to set up of a wagon factory in the State at present.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) ALLOCATION OF RICE TO KERALA .
records.name: P.J. Kurien
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has reduced the quantity of rice allocated to Kerala, through public distribution system;

(b) if so, the details alongwith the reasons therefor;

(c) whether the Government of Kerala has requested for enhancing the rice allocation to Kerala; and

(d) if so, Government`s reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)


(a) & (b): Yes Sir. A uniform decision to rationalize rice allocation from the Central Pool stocks for the APL category under the Targeted Public Distribution System has been implemented w.e.f. April 2007 on the basis of a particular State`s maximum monthly offtake during last three years i.e. 2003-04; 2004-05 and 2005-06. This has been made applicable to all States, including Kerala.

(c) & (d): Yes Sir. The Government has made an adhoc/additional/festival of allocation of 51,000 MT of rice and 83,778 MT of wheat to State of Kerala during the current year in addition to normal allocations made under the TPDS.

records.qtitle: FOODGRAINS STOCK FOR PDS .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether country would experience a tight position in foodgrains stock in the Central pool for the public distribution system by April, 2009; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)

(a) & (b): Because of lower procurement of wheat and rice than their requirements under TPDS, welfare schemes and for calamity relief etc., the buffer stock of wheat and rice available in the Central Pool on 01.01.2008 has been less than the minimum buffer norms. records.qtitle: CONSTITUTION OF FARMERS DEBT RELIEF COMMISSION .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to constitute a Farmers Debt Relief Commission;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) if not, the reasons therefor;

(d) whether Government is also considering to write off the debts of small and marginal farmers and bring down the interest on farm loans to a simple interest; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a)to(c): There is no proposal with the Government of India for constitution of a Farmers Debt Relief Commission because the Government has taken several initiatives for providing debt relief to the farmers.

(d): Yes, Sir.

(e): Details are annexed.

ANNEXURE

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PART (e) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1564 TO BE ANSWERED ON 14.03.2008 BY SHRI ABDUL WAHAB PEEVEE AND SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN REGARDING “CONSTITUTION OF FARMERS DEBT RELIEF COMMISSION”.

A scheme of Debt Waiver and Debt Relief for farmers has been announced in the Union Budget 2008-09. The salient features of the proposed scheme are :

(i) All agricultural loans disbursed by scheduled commercial banks, regional rural banks and cooperative credit institutions up to March 31, 2007 and overdue as on December 31, 2007 will be covered under the scheme.

(ii) For marginal farmers (i.e., holding upto 1 hectare) and small farmers (1-2 hectare), there will be a complete waiver of all loans that were overdue on December 31, 2007 and which remained unpaid until February 29, 2008. In respect of other farmers, there will be a One Time Settlement (OTS) scheme for all loans that were overdue on December 31, 2007 and which remained unpaid until February 29, 2008. Under the OTS, a rebate of 25 per cent will be given against payment of the balance of 75 per cent.

(iii) Agricultural loans which were restructured and rescheduled by banks in 2004 and 2006 through special packages and other loans rescheduled in the normal course as per RBI guidelines, will also be eligible either for a waiver or OTS on the same pattern.

(iv) The implementation of the debt waiver and debt relief scheme will be completed by June 30, 2008. Upon being granted debt waiver or signing an agreement for debt relief under the OTS, the farmer would be entitled to fresh agricultural loans from the banks in accordance with normal rules.

(v) It is estimated that about 3 crore small and marginal farmers and about 1 crore other farmers will be benefited under the proposed scheme. The total value of overdue loans being waived is estimated at Rs.50,000 crore and the OTS relief on the overdue loans is estimated at Rs.10,000 crore.

2. Considering that high rates of interest often act as a deterrent to farmers from availing farm credit, it was announced in the Union Budget (2006-07), that crop loans upto Rs.3 lakh would be given at 7% rate of interest. Accordingly, crop loans are presently being made available at 7% at the ground level by almost all banks with interest subvention from the Government of India. This scheme is continued for 2007-08 and 2008-09 also.

records.qtitle: REVIEW OF SPICES AND PLANTATION SECTOR IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to review the spices and plantation sector in Kerala in the near future;

(b) whether any plan has been chalked out to invest Rs. 5,000 crore in Kerala’s agriculture sector; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a) to (c): The spices and plantation sectors in the country including in the State of Kerala are receiving constant attention of the Government. For overall development of these sectors, a number of Plan Schemes are being implemented by the Government through Commodity Boards, under which financial/technical assistance is provided for development of these Sectors. As an ongoing process, the schemes are monitored and reviewed from time to time. Some of the important programmes in the plantation and agriculture sector are as given below:-

Tea: Government has already launched in January, 2007 a Special Purpose Tea Fund (SPTF) to extend financial support to the tea growers to take up replanting and rejuvenation of the old tea areas. The scheme envisages accelerating the pace of replanting and rejuvenation by ensuring availability of funds to the extent of 75% of the unit cost by way of long term loan (50%) and subsidy (25%). The growers are required to bring in 25% of the total cost.

Coffee: The Government has proposed a similar scheme for coffee replantation, on the lines of SPTF for the revival of old and senile coffee plantations which are uneconomical in the present conditions. Coffee Board has identified about 80,000 hectares of coffee area out of total of 3.81 lakhs hectares, which are uneconomical and requires to be replanted to improve farm productivity to desired levels in the long run. An outlay of Rs. 180.00 crore has been proposed by the Coffee Board in the 11th Plan for this purpose.

Rubber: Rubber Board has formulated a proposal for replanting 33,500 hectare of old and uneconomical rubber plantations in the country with an outlay of around Rs. 50.00 crore in the 11th Plan for payment of planting grant @ 25% of the development cost.

Spices: Spices Board have submitted a proposal for replantation and rejuvenation of cardamom plantation on the lines of SPTF for tea with a subsidy component of Rs. 211.35 crore covering about 65,000 hectares for small and large cardamom plantation under the 11th Plan.

There is a proposal for replantation/rejuvenation of about 2 lakh hectares of pepper in Kerala over a period of ten years under the National Horticulture Mission at an estimated cost of Rs.300.00 crores.

Cashew: It is proposed to undertake rejuvenation programmes of cashew in 6 cashew growing States during XI Plan under National Horticulture Measures at an estimated cost of Rs.30.00 crores.

Coconut: There is a proposal with Department of Agriculture for replanting and rejuvenation of coconut gardens in traditional coconut growing States to cover an area of 4.56 lakh hectares with total estimated project cost of Rs.4,766.66 crores over a span of 6-7 years with financial assistance to the extent of Rs.1358.62 crores.

records.qtitle: EPIDEMICS IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether a number of viral hepatitis and fever epidemic cases have been noticed in Kerala in the recent past;

(b) if so, the number of persons died, so far;

(c) whether any Central team has been sent to Kerala to find out the reasons for the disease; and

(d) the nature of assistance provided to the State by the Centre?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) &(b) Sporadic outbreaks of chickungunya have been reported from Kerala since July 2006. However, no death due to chickungunya has been reported. The cases of dengue fever have also been reported in Kerala in recent past and 5 deaths in 2006 and 8 deaths in 2007 (till 12th August) have been reported due to dengue.

The State of Kerala has also reported 12720 cases and 12 deaths due to Viral Hepatitis during 2006.

(c) Four central teams have been sent to Kerala for investigation of the outbreak during the period from May 2007 to July 2007. The teams observed that the fever cases were mainly due to chickungunya. The occurrence of the disease is related to climatic conditions such as rainfall, temperature and humidity and high vector density.

(d) Under National Vector Borne Diseases Control Programme(NVBDCP) implemented by Government of India, regular logistics like adulticides and larvicides are supplied to the State. In addition, an amount of Rs.220.5 lakhs was released to Kerala during 2006-07 as emergency package for prevention and control of Chickungunya towards the purchase of fogging machines, Pyrethrum extract, Insecticide treated bednets etc. An amount of Rs.403.90 lakhs has been allotted as emergency package for Kerala during 2007-08 also. Technical guidance has also been provided to Kerala for diagnostic facilities.

To strengthen surveillance activities and to promote early detection of outbreak & institute appropriate action for prevention and control of epidemic and other diseases, an Integrated Disease Surveillance Project is in existence since 2004. The programme is being implemented in phased manner and Kerala has already been covered in Phase-I of the project.

records.qtitle: BOOSTING HORTICULTURE EXPORT .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country produces nearly eleven per cent of all the world`s vegetables and fifteen per cent of all fruits, yet its share in global exports of vegetables is only 1.7 per cent and in fruits, a meager 0.5 per cent only;

(b) if so, what are the major factors which are undermining out country`s potential for reaching super markets around the globe; and

(c) the steps taken by Government to boost horticulture export?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a): As per production database of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) for the year 2005, India`s share in global production of vegetables and fruits was about 9.2% and 10.47% respectively and the share in global export of vegetables and fruits was about 3.72% and 0.36% respectively.

(b): The major factors undermining India`s potential for exports are: - 



1.	Unorganized export sector. 

2.	Lack of standards for farm & orchard maintenance including presence of pest and disease. 

3.	Lack of packaging standards. 

4.	Lack of market information.  

5.	Poor harvest infrastructure.
6.	Lack of proper cold chain and logistics facilities. 

7	Various non-tariff barriers imposed by importing countries, particularly, the developed 
	countries. 

8.	Lack of awareness among farmers about producing good quality and safe produce. 

9.	Lack of trained Horticulture manpower.
10.	High transport costs.


(c):	 The steps taken by Government to boost horticulture exports are:-


1.	Training programmes for improvement in quality of produce and developed pre-harvest and 
	post harvest protocols for export of grapes, mangoes, litchis, oranges, apples, Kinnows etc. 


2.	Export standards for 34 fruits and vegetables to EU have been prepared and notified under the 
	Agmark Act.


3.	Schemes for registration/ recognition of Pack houses/ processing units have been introduced 
	for fresh fruits and vegetables particularly mangoes and grapes, meat, poultry, dairy, 
	floriculture, peanuts, rice and cereal sectors. 


4.	A Scheme for grant of license to use certification mark ` Quality Produce of India` is in 
	operation for the processing/export.

  

5.	 Promoting commercial research for benefit of processors/exporters under its scheme for 
Research & Development through     various organizations under ICAR/CSIR system and 
Agriculture Universities. Creation of awareness among the farmers regarding orchard 
practices for qualitative production has been undertaken.


6.	Further the Department of Commerce   through APEDA is implementing the concept of Agri 
Export zones (AEZ) which aims at overall development of the supply and value chain of the 
identified commodities in a contiguous geographical region, having export potential, in 
collaboration with the State and Central Government agencies. 


7    The Government of India promotes agro-exports directly and through Commodity Boards, 
Export Promotion Councils and Commodity Associations.  In order to boost export of agro 
products, the Government, provides various incentives for infrastructure development, quality 
control, market development and promotion, packaging, publicity, information dissemination 
etc. besides providing assistance to exporters for conducting publicity campaigns, market 
surveys, sending delegations abroad, participating in international trade fairs, inviting 
potential buyers etc.  Further, initiatives include awareness amongst farmers about the latest 
techniques of farming through mass media support to agriculture   through Doordarshan. In 
order to disseminate information on improved production technologies amongst the farmers, 
block demonstrations and Integrated Pest Management (IPM) demonstrations are organized 
through State Department of Agriculture and Frontline Demonstrations through Indian 
Council of Agricultural Research.


8.    The Government has introduced a number of initiatives and interventions for enhancement of 
production and productivity of agricultural products, which inter-alia include Integrated 
Schemes under National Horticulture Mission for integrated Development of Horticulture, 
and Micro-irrigation.

(a) Yes, Sir. There are two ongoing projects in Kerala State with loans from Asian Development Bank. records.qtitle: POWER SHORTAGE IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Prime Minister has expressed his serious concern over power shortage of varying degrees across the country and suggested introspection on crisis in power sector; and

(b) if so, the various measures under Government`s consideration to tackle the power shortage?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )


(a) : Yes, Sir, while presenting the National Awards to the Power Utilities, for meritorious performance, Hon`ble Prime Minister has expressed concern over power shortages and suggested introspection on crisis in the power sector.

(b) : The following steps have been taken/are being taken to improve overall availability of power in the country: 




(i)		Rigorous monitoring of capacity addition of the on-going generation projects.


(ii)	Advance planning of generation capacity addition projects for the 11th Five Year Plan.


(iii)	Implementation of Ultra Mega Power Projects of 4000 MW each to achieve benefit of 
economy of scale.


(iv)	`Partnership in Excellence` Programme starting with adoption of better operation and 
maintenance (O&M) practices to enable enhancement of Plant Load Factor (PLF) of 
existing thermal power stations through tie-up with well performing power utilities as a 
pre-cursor to renovation and modernization.


(v)	Renovation, modernization and life extension of old and inefficient generation units with 
interest subsidy on loans by the Power Finance Corporation and Rural Electrification 
Corporation under `Accelerated Generation and Supply Programme (AG&SP).


(vi)		Tapping of surplus power from captive power plants.


(vii)	Utilization of unutilized capacity of gas based stations on liquid fuel.


(viii)	Strengthening/Augmentation of sub-transmission system in State under Accelerated 
Power Development Reforms Programme (APDRP) as a major step towards reduction 
of Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) Losses.


(ix)	Coordinated operation and maintenance of hydro, thermal, nuclear and gas based 
power stations to optimally utilize the existing generation capacity.


(x)	Optimum utilization of available power by strengthening of inter-state and inter-regional 
transmission capacity.


(xi)	Promoting demand side management, energy efficiency and energy conservation 
measures.


(xii)	Rigorous monitoring of production, transportation and supply of coal by an Inter-
Ministerial Group comprising representatives of Ministry of Coal, Ministry of Power, 
Ministry of Railways, Central Electricity Authority and Coal India Limited on weekly / 
fortnightly basis to review and resolve the constraints


(xiii)	Procurement of hydro-electric power from Bhutan.

records.qtitle: ATHIRAPPILLY HYDRO ELECTRIC PROJECT .
