( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) to (d) : Athirappilly Hydro Electric Project (163 MW) was accorded Techno- Economic Clearance (TEC) by Central Electricity Authority (CEA) on 31st March, 2005 at an estimated cost of Rs. 385.6 crores at April, 2004 price level. The environmental clearance for the above project was accorded on 20.1.1998. However, the environmental clearance was suspended on the basis of a judgment (17.10.2001) of the Hon`ble High Court of Kerala. The court had directed to conduct the public hearing. The public hearing was conducted by Kerala State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB) on 6.2.2002 on the basis of an Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) report prepared with eight months data against one year`s data required for river valley projects and proceedings were submitted to Ministry of Environment and Forests

(MoEF). The public hearing panel had recommended for 2nd public hearing with a comprehensive EIA. On a request from the State Government for not insisting upon 2nd public hearing, the issue was reviewed by the MoEF and the proposal placed before the Expert Committee. Environmental clearance for the project was restored on 10.2.2002 subject to strict compliance to certain terms and conditions.

Four Public Interest Litigations (PILs) were filed before the Hon`ble High Court of Kerala against the grant of environmental clearance and implementation of the project. The Hon`ble High Court delivered its judgment on 23.3.2006 quashing the environment clearance of the project and directed the KSPCB to conduct the public hearing afresh after publishing the EIA report and complete the same within two months. The public hearing was conducted by the KSPCB on 15th June, 2006 and the report has been submitted to MoEF on 22nd July, 2006. The proposal was considered by the Environment Appraisal Committee (EAC) in its meetings held on 23rd August, 2006 and 15th November, 2006. On receipt of further representations, a Sub-Committee of EAC has visited the proposed site during April, 2007.

records.qtitle: ARIS IN KERALA
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of steps taken by Government to promote agro-based industries in Kerala;

(b) the details of rural industries under implementation in the State; and

(c) the details of funds allocated, sanctioned, released and utilised for the purpose during the last three years, year-wise?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES

(SHRI MAHABIR PRASAD)

(a): The Government (in the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries) has been promoting the agro-based rural industries throughout the country, including Kerala, by implementing the following schemes: 



(i)	Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP), through the Khadi 
and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), to help eligible entrepreneurs to set 
up village industry units and thus create employment opportunities in village 
and small towns with population upto 20,000.  Under this programme, 
entrepreneurs can establish village industries by availing the margin money 
assistance from KVIC and loans from public sector scheduled commercial banks, 
selected regional rural banks, cooperative banks, etc., for projects with a 
maximum cost of Rs. 25 lakh.  


(ii)	Rural Industries Service Centres Scheme (RISC), through the KVIC, 
for setting up of common facility centres (CFCs) to provide infrastructural 
support and services to such industries;


(iii)	Product Development, Design Intervention and Packaging Programme 
(PRODIP), through the KVIC, for improved designs and packaging of khadi and 
village industry (KVI) products;


(iv)	Development of Production Infrastructure, through Coir Board, for 
development of production infrastructure, whereunder financial assistance for 
setting up of new coir units at the rate of 25 per cent of the cost of equipment 
and infrastructural facilities subject to a ceiling of Rs. 1.5 lakh for setting 
coir units and Rs. 50,000 for modernisation of existing coir units and for 
installation of generator sets of upto 11 KVA capacity to run fibre/curled coir 
units.




(v)	Mahila Coir Yojana, through the Coir Board, for providing 
trainings in spinning to women artisans and for providing subsidy of 75 per cent 
of the cost of the ratt 


(vi)	Modernisation of Extraction and Processing of Coir Fibre, through 
the Coir Board, for intensification of research and development efforts for 
introducing new technology for extraction and processing of coir fibre, 
development of machinery, product diversification, introduction of new products, 
etc.


(b):  The rural industries under the REGP are promoted under the 
following seven broad categories: 


(i)	Mineral Based Industry, 

(ii)	Forest Based Industry, 

(iii)	Agro and Food Processing Industry, 

(iv)	Polymer and 
Chemical Based Industry, 

(v)	Rural Engineering and Bio Technology 
Industry, 

(vi)	Handmade Paper & Fibre industry, 

(vii)	Service activities.
	 The details of value of production and sales and the employment 
generated under
seven broad categories during  2005-06, in Kerala are as under:

records.qtitle: FLOOD AND DROUGHT LOSS IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of representations received from the Government of Kerala claiming compensation for agricultural loss due to floods and droughts during the last three years, year-wise;

(b) the details of assistance sought, assistance approved and released in each case;

(c) the status of pending representations;

(d) whether Kerala Government has also sought assistance for revival of agriculture sector; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a) to (e): For the drought of 2003-04, the Government of Kerala had submitted two Memoranda, one in January 2004 and the other in April, 2004, seeking assistance of Rs.1359.03 crores and Rs.2844.90 crores, respectively, from the National Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF), for drought relief. However, no assistance was released from the NCCF as the balance in the Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) account of the State was more than the amount approved by the High Level Committee (HLC).
In July, 2004, the State Government had submitted a Memorandum seeking assistance of Rs.3847 crores for revival of Agriculture Sector, which included requirement towards input subsidy for damaged crops. A multi-disciplinary team had visited the State for assessment of requirements etc. Taking into account its recommendations and based on approval by the Prime Minister, Rs.106 crores was released to the State from the NCCF towards input subsidy for damaged crops.

Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is concerned with matters relating to floods. According to them, the State Government had sought assistance of Rs.196.40 crores from the NCCF for the floods of 2005. An amount of Rs.17.94 crores from the NCCF was released during floods of 2005 on an `on account` basis. However, based on the approval of the High Level Committee (HLC), an amount of Rs.12.72 crores was identified as excess against the `on account` payment. According to MHA, the excess amount is to be adjusted against the State Government`s long-term requirement of funds. For the floods of 2006, as against the requirement of Rs.149.08 crores from the NCCF projected by the State Government, no amount was released from the NCCF as 75% of balance available in CRF of the State for the instant calamity was more than the amount approved by the HLC.

records.qtitle: NHS IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the length of National Highways in Kerala and the total amount spent on their maintenance and upkeep during the last three years, year-wise;

(b) the proposals pending for upgradation of State Highways into National Highways; and

(c) the status of each proposal?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS


(SHRI K. H. MUNIYAPPA)

(a) The length of National Highways (NHs) in Kerala is 1526 km. The amount spent on their upkeep and maintenance during the last 3 years starting from 2004-05 is Rs. 31.83 crore, Rs. 55.45 crore and Rs. 19.89 crore respectively.

(b & c) There is only one proposal received from the Government of Kerala for declaring the State road as National Highway. At present, declaration of new roads as National Highway is not the priority of the Government. The emphasis is on improvement of the existing National Highways to NH standards.

records.qtitle: NRI INVESTMENT PROPOSALS FOR KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have approved any NRI investment proposals for Kerala in the last three year, year-wise; and

(b) if so, the status of each proposal?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS

(SHRI VAYALAR RAVI)

(a)&(b) The nodal Ministry dealing with approval of investment in India, including by non-resident Indians, is the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion. Implementation of such investment proposals approved is monitored by the State Government concerned. The information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.

records.qtitle: NRIS AS IIT DIRECTORS .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the reason: for the IIT Directors in many places and especially in Kharakpur being an NRI and whether due to their NRI status most of the time they are staying outside; if` so. the reasons therefor;

(b) the number of Directors staying within the campus with their families;

(c) the authority responsible for maintenance of the approach road to the campus; and

(d) whether his Minister have taken any initiative to improve the pathetic condition of the road?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANIIESWARI)

(a) & (b) None of the Directors of the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) is an NRI. The Directors stay within the campus or` in the city where the IIT is located.

(c) & (d) Central/State Government Public Works Departments and local municipalities are responsible for maintenance of the approach roads to end around the Institutes. They are approached by the Institute authorities as and when contingencies arise.

records.qtitle: MINISTER S QUOTA IN ADMISSION IN KENDRIYA VIDYALAYAS .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether, apart from two admissions in Kendriya Vidyalayas for each M.P., is there any priorities from the Ministers quota for admission in Kendriya Vidyalayas for children who are seeking admission through M.P.`s quota; and

(b) if so, the details thereof`?.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M. A. A. FATMI)

(a) & (b) Each Member of Parliament (MP) can refer two cases for admission in an academic year in any Kendriya Vidyalaya in the country for all classes except class X and XII. The discretionary quota of the Chairman, Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan, is exercised in respect of the priority fixed for the purpose.

records.qtitle: PROCUREMENT OF RESERVED AND UNRESERVED TICKETS .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Southern Railway did not follow the purchase order specification while accepting the unreserved tickets printed from the private firm during the first quarter of this year ;

(b) whether this firm is supplying the sub-standard unreserved tickets to other zonal Railways as well;

(c) whether there is any complaint pending against the firm;

(d) if so, what is the action taken thereon; and

(e) whether there is any policy set by his Ministry for procurement of reserved and unreserved railway tickets?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU)

(a) No, Sir.

(b) No, Sir

(c) No. Sir.

(d) Does not arise.

(e) Yes, Sir.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPMENT OF NHS IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any proposal is under consideration of Government for the development of highways and other roads in Kerala, the expenditure of which does not fall under any of Golden Quadrilateral or the North-South, East-West corridor project; and

(b) if so, the status report in each case?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS


(SHRI K. H. MUNIYAPPA)


(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Seventeen works amounting to Rs.620.00 crore were sanctioned during 2006-07 for the development of National Highways in Kerala, which are in various stages of progress. In addition, 3 works to be taken up under NHDP Phase III are presently at DPR stage. For other roads, 4 works amounting to Rs. 28.50 crore and one work amounting to Rs. 14.24 crore were sanctioned under CRF and Inter State Connectivity respectively during the same period, which are also in various stages of progress.

records.qtitle: NEW RAILWAY ZONE IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any representation from the Kerala Government for a new railway zone in the State; and

(b) if so, what is the response thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

( SHRI R. VELU )


(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) New Railway Zones are set up keeping in view the factors like size, workload, accessibility, traffic pattern and other operational / administrative requirements etc. consistent with the needs of economy and efficiency and not on regional considerations. The proposal for creation of new Zone, in Kerala, when examined in the light of these considerations, has not been found feasible.

records.qtitle: CRITERIA FOR CLEARANCE UNDER FCRA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the FCRA clearance is not given to Institutions/ orphanages, fearing the funds may go to some kind of terrorist activities;

(b) if so, whether the institutions who are already having the FCRA clearance, are eligible to receive funds from abroad; and

(c) what are the guidelines for the applicants who apply for fresh FCRA clearance?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) to (c) : A Statement is laid on the table of the House

Statement in reply to PART (a) TO (c) OF Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1718 for 14th March, 2007 by Shri Abdul Wahab Peevee regarding Criteria for clearance under FCRA.

(a) No Sir.

(b) The associations which are already registered can receive foreign funds if they are not prohibited from receiving Foreign contribution or placed in the Prior Permission category by the Central Government.

(c) The organizations seeking foreign contributions for definite cultural, social, economic, educational or religious programmes may either obtain registration or prior permission to receive foreign contribution from the Ministry of Home Affairs by making an application in the prescribed format and furnishing details of the activities and audited accounts. The registration is granted only to such associations, which have a proven track record of functioning in the chosen field of work during last three years. Registration is granted only after thorough security vetting of the activities and antecedents of the organisation and office bearers thereof. After registration, such organisation is free to receive foreign contribution from any foreign source for the stated objectives.

However, such organizations which are newly established and do not have a proven track record of functioning may also receive foreign contribution for specific activities, for a specific purpose and from a specific source after seeking project based Prior Permission (PP) from the Ministry of Home Affairs.

To put in place a user-friendly and transparent service delivery system, the website of MHA has been uploaded with FC(R) Act, 1976, Rules, FC forms, common grounds for rejection of cases, check list for ensuring proper filling of forms, illustrative list of activities permitted to be carried out by associations, etc.

records.qtitle: DISPUTES OVER MULLAPERIYAR RIVER
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have initiated discussion at the level of Chief Ministers of Kerala and Karnataka for finding a solution to the dispute over Mullaperiyar Water;

(b) if so, what are the results thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that Kerala has agreed to give water to Tamil Nadu as before and wanted a new Dam to be constructed at Mullaperiyar for ensuring safety of life and properties of people of Kerala, at least in several districts of Kerala; and

(d) what is the present stage of talk which has been dead locked and what further initiative is being contemplated by the Centre?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

( SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV)  

(a) to (b) The Hon’ble Union Minister (WR) convened an inter-State meeting of the Chief Ministers of States of Tamil Nadu and Kerala on Mullaperiyar dam issue on 29.11.2006 at New Delhi. The meeting was attended by the Chief Ministers, Ministers (WR/PW) of the two States as well as Senior Officers of the Ministry of Water Resources, Central Water Commission and States of Tamil Nadu & Kerala. The States of Tamil Nadu & Kerala reiterated their respective stands in the meeting. They have also agreed to discuss the issue further in a meeting under the auspices of Hon’ble Union Minister (WR) with the Ministers (WR/PW) from the States of Tamil Nadu & Kerala.

(c) Chief Minister of Kerala made a statement in the meeting that proposal of Government of Kerala to have a new dam as a replacement to the old dam would provide water to the people of Tamil Nadu and remove the shadow of fear from the minds of people of Kerala.

(d) As decided in the meeting on 29.11.2006, Union Minister for Water Resources convened another inter-State meeting on 18.12.2006 of Minister of (PW/WR) of Tamil Nadu and Kerala in which no solution acceptable to both the States emerged.

records.qtitle: NON SUPPLY OF SGRY FOODGRAINS IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that the foodgrains allotted to the Kerala Government under SGRY Scheme has not been supplied to the concerned DRDAs/Panchayats for distribution to the people;

(b) if so, what action has been taken in the matter; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL)


(a) to (c) The Government of Kerala has informed that a new system of distribution of foodgrains through extensive network of `Maveli` and `Sabari` stores under the Kerala State Civil Supplies Corporation to BPL Ration Card holders has been introduced. In view of the time taken to operationalize this decision, there has been delay in lifting of foodgrains by District Rural Development Agencies. The State Government has further informed that now all the details have been finalized and the lifting process would start immediately.

records.qtitle: MINORITY EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS UNDER RESERVATION
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that some States including Kerala have attended the Chief Minister`s and Education Ministers` conference held at Delhi recently and requested the Central Government to bring minority educational institutions under the preview of the proposed legislation on reservation in unaided educational institutions; and

(b) if so, what is the Government`s stand in this matter.`?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): Article 15(5) of the Constitution exempts minority educational institutions established
under Article 30(1) thereof from laws for the advancement of the weaker sections in matters of
admission.

records.qtitle: OVERSEAS INDIAN CENTRE AT DUBAI .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have decided to give approval to set up Overseas Indian Centre at Dubai;

(b) if so, the details of facilities the overseas Indians can expect from this centre;

(c) whether there is any proposal from Government to start such centres in other parts of the Gulf region;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS

(SHRI VAYALAR RAVI)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b)to(e) The Overseas Indian Centre at Dubai would provide medical, legal and financial counseling etc. to the overseas Indian workers in the Gulf countries. At present, there is no proposal to set up another such centre in the Gulf region.

records.qtitle: LAPSE IN THE SECURITY OF PRIME MINISTER S CONVOY .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Central Government have asked for a report from the Kerala Government in regard to security lapses that the Prime Minister`s convoy took a wrong route during his recent visit to that State; if so, what is the report; and

(b) what steps the Central Government have taken to avoid such incidents in future?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL )

(a): Yes, Sir. The Government of Kerala has viewed this security lapse very seriously and placed the Pilot Officer under suspension. Further, the IGP (Security) and Commissioner of Police, Thiruvananthapuram were also transferred out from their respective posts. Besides the Government of Kerala is also making all efforts to ensure foolproof security arrangements for VVIPs in the State.


(b): The Central Government has been advising all the State/UT Governments to strictly implement all the security guidelines circulated by this Ministry earlier in order to avoid recurrence of such incidents in future.

records.qtitle: STATE LEVEL MINORITY COMMISSION .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that some States are not showing interest to set up Statelevel Minority Commission; if so, the details of such States;

(b) the steps taken by Government to set up State level Commissions;

(c) Whether a conference of Minority Commissions was held at Delhi recently;and

(d) if so, the details of subjects discussed and the outcome there of;
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS

( A.R. ANTULAY)

(a) and (b): State Governments~ which have not yet set upstate Minority Commissions are, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Kerala, Meghalaya, Mizoram Nagaland, Orissa, Punjab, Sikkim and Tripura.
The concerned State Governments have been advised on a number of occasions to take appropriate action in the matter.

(e) and (d): The National Commission for Minorities convened the 5th Annual Conference of State Minorities Commissions at New Delhi on 2n~ November, 2006. Amongst the major issues discussed in the Conference were the following:- 

	
(i)	Minorities should feel safe and get a fair and reasonable 
share &development.

	
(ii)	Communal peace and harmony should be maintained. 


(iii) Special tribunals should be set up to deal with communal offences.



(iv) The victims of communal carnage should be given adequate financial 
support for rehabilitation.



(v)    Minorities should get a fair share in Central and State 
Government jobs, both in the public and private sectors.



(vi) Lack of access to the common school system is maintv responsible 
for the socioeconomic backwardness of the minority communities, particularly 
the muslim community and muslim girls. A thrust for education is to be made for 
the blocks and districts having a predominantly Muslim population and widening 
of access to professional and technical education.



(vii) Government should monitor- implementation of the Prime Minister`s 
New I5 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities.



(viii) The scholarship schemes funded by the Maulana Azad Education-
Foundation should be enlarged to cover the post-matric level also.




	(ix)	The WakfBoard properties should be utilized to open educational 
institutions.

	(x)	The status of the National Commission for Minorities should be 
raised to a constitutional body.




	The Prime Minister`s New 15 Point Programme tbr the Welfare of
 Minorities~ announced in June, 2006 addresses many of these concerns.

records.qtitle: CONTINUING EDUCATION PROGRAMME IN KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the amount given as grant-in-aid to each State under the Continuing Education Programme under the National Literacy Mission;

(b) the amount sanctioned for Kerala alongwith the amount released so far and still to be released; and

(c) whether there is any separate programme for the SCs/STs under the National Literacy Mission?
records.ans_text:
MINISTEN OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. KANTI SINGH)

(a) A statement showing State-wise grant released under Continuing Education Programme during the last three years is at Annexure-A.

(b) Under the Scheme of Continuing Education, the Central Government provides 100 per cent financial assistance for implementation of the Scheme for the first three years of the project. An amount of Rs.32.79 crore has been released for the`, first three project years and the entire amount has been released as the 100 per cent Central assistance. For the 4th and 5th year of the project, the Central Government and State Government are required to share the expenditure in the ratio of 50:50 An amount of Rs.12.10 crore is estimated for 4th and 5th project years as the Central share.

(c) There is no separate programme for SCs/STs under National Literacy Mission. However, all Schemes of NLM seek to cover illiterate adult population in 15-35 age group including SCs/STs.

records.qtitle: . NATIONAL ELIGIBILITY TEST .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have reviewed the procedure followed, by UGC in conducting National Eligibility Test;

(b) whether it is a fact that it has lost standards required and is doing injustice to M. Phil/Ph. D. holders;

(c) whether Government have any plan to give exceptions to M.Phil/Ph.D holders from the Central Universities in case of NET; and

(d) the policy followed by UGC in granting Deemed University status to the institutes and colleges in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN :RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI KANTI SINGH)
(a} to (c) : In order to consider various suggestions made from time to time by teacher`s organizations and educationists, a Committee has been constituted by the Government to review the National Eligibility Test (NET) for its utility, effectiveness and continuation.
(d):The University Grants Commission (UGC) has made detailed guidelines for considering proposals for declaring an institution as deemed to be university under Section 3 of the UGC Act. The institutions which conform to these guidelines are recommended by the UGC to the Government for granting the status of deemed university.

records.qtitle: EX SERVICE MEN AS SECURITY PERSONNEL IN BSNL KERALA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Ex-service men employed as security personnel by BSNL in Kerala are not permanent employees and they are thrown out any time;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) what Government propose to do on the matter?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) & (b) The Ex-service men employed as security personnel in Kerala are not BSNL employees. As per the prevailing policy of Government of India regarding resettlement of Ex-servicemen, BSNL is required to obtain contract security service, through Ex-service men security agencies sponsored by the Directorate General of Resettlement, Ministry of Defence. The Directorate General of Resettlement does not sponsor any agency on permanent basis. There is change of security agencies/security personnel on the expiry of the contract period.

(c) Does not arise in view of (a) & (b) above.

records.qtitle: LOKPAL BILL
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to bring forward Lokpal Bill during the current session of Parliament which is pending legislation for the last 36 years;

(a) whether certain social activists of the Lok Sevak Sangh and other organisations reportedly have threatened to undertake `fast unto death` over this inordinate delay in legislation of above mentioned Bill; and

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto alongwith reasons for delay?

records.qtitle: CONTROVERSY OVER CENSUS DATA .
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:

(SHRI MANIKRAO HODLYA GAVIT)


(a)&(b): Yes, Sir. An internal inquiry has been made. A mistake has been committed in the Report on Religion data released on 6th September, 2004. It was not mentioned in the Brief Analysis that the growth rates were based on unadjusted figures. Appropriate warning is being issued to the concerned.

(a) Yes, Sir. Licences have been issued to various operators including PSUs to provide mobile services throughout India. As per licence agreement they are to provide mobile services in 50% of the district headquarters or any other town in lieu of District Headquarter within three years of the effective date of licence.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(DR. RAGHUVANSH PRASAD SINGH)

(a) The unit for coverage under PMGSY is `habitation` and not `village`. A habitation is deemed to be connected if it lies on all-weather road or is within 500 metres from a connected habitation or an all-weather road. The Government of Kerala has reported that 118 unconnected habitations with population more than thousand in the State are likely to be covered under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY).

(b) An amount of Rs.20.00 crore has been allocated for Kerala under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana in the current year.

records.qtitle: ISLAND SPECIAL ALLOWANCE
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.ans_text:
FINANCE MINISTER

(SHRI P.CHIDAMBARAM)

(a), (b), (c) & (d): A Statement is laid on the table of the House.

Statement referred to in reply to parts (a), (b), (c) & (d) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No 186 for 14.12.2004 tabled by Shri Abdul Wahab Peevee regarding Island Special Allowance.

(a), (b) & (c):- Two types of Special Allowances are paid to the Bank employees posted in Andaman & Nicobar Islands namely, the Adhoc and Temporary Incentive and the Special Area Allowance. The Adhoc and Temporary Incentive is paid only to officers who are transferred from other parts of the country and posted to Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Special Area Allowance is paid to all employees. Thus, so far as the Special Area Allowance is concerned the staff officer’s belonging to these islands are on ml equal footing vis-a-vis their counterparts from the mainland. Since the staff posted from the mainland to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have to leave their families behind and manage double establishments, the ad-hoc and temporary incentive is given as an incentive to them. The same is not given to local staff as they continue to work in, the same social, cultural and ethnic environment.

(d):-As per a quick estimate, the additional cost of giving Ad-hoc and Temporary Incentive to the Islanders would be approximately Rs.30 lakhs per annum.

records.qtitle: APPOINTMENT OF WELFARE OFFICER FOR NRIS
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have decided to appoint Welfare Officers in countries with high density of NRIs and people of Indian Origin to help Indian families to find antecedents of prospective grooms;

(b) whether it is a fact that thousands of girls have been lured into marriage by boys claiming to be well-settled abroad and after marriage disappeared or abandoned their wives;

(c) if so, the details of such cases available with Government, State-wise;

(d) whether Government have any plan to provide help to such Indian girls who have no where to go in a foreign land; and

(e) if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINSTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS

(SHRI JAGDISH TYTLER)
a) No.
b) & c) Though it is generally believed that there are large number of such cases, only a few case have been brought to the specific notice of the Government.
d) & e) There already exists a system of redressal for such problems in Indian Mission abroad. Whenever they receive a complaint of torture and desertion of Indian wives by the NRI husbands, they render assistance to the victim by way of trying to reason with the spouse with a view to bring about an amicable settlement. In the case of unresponding spouses, they give a patient hearing and sympathetic counseling to the victims, provide consular assistance and extend humanitarian aid, if necessary, with the assistance of the local Indian community. Ways and means of supplementing this with legal advice, verification of the antecedents of the grooms, compulsory registration of the marriages, etc are under consideration of Government.

records.qtitle: REVIEW OF ECONOMIC POLICIES
records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) the various steps undertaken by Government to generate employment opportunities in the country;

(b) whether Government propose to review the impact of its economic polices including labour laws on the growth of employment; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI K. CHANDRASEKHAR RAO)
a) Government is targeting creation of 5 crore employment opportunities during the 10th Plan period by focusing on the following areas. 8% growth with business as usual will contribute around 3 crore employment opportunities. Special employment generation programmes will yield 2 crore employment opportunities. Special emphasis on agriculture, irrigation, agro-forestry, small and medium enterprises, information communication technology, tourism and other services. b&c) Government had reviewed all aspects of growth of employment in the 10th Plan document. The approach to 10th Plan focusses on providing gainful high quality employment to the additions to the labour force and it is listed as one of the monitorable objectives for the 10th Plan and beyond. The growth strategy of 10th Plan has laid emphasis on rapid growth of those sectors which are likely to create high quality employment opportunities and deal with the policy constraints which discourage growth of employment. Particular attention has been paid to the policy environment influencing a wide range of economic activities, which have a large employment potential.

(b) Proposals to the value of Rs.97.89 crore have been cleared for construction of 270 road works with a length of 493.65 km in Kerala since the inception of PMGSY in 2000-01. As per reports received from the State upto October 2004, they have incurred an expenditure of Rs. 52.45 crore and completed construction of 275.41 km of roads. While 270 road works have been cleared, only 144 have been completed up to October 2004.
